statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-47303 (GHSA-2p3q-h3hg-jcqq) is an elevation of privilege issue in the ASP.NET Core Negotiate authentication handler caused by improper parsing. Microsoft lists only the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate NuGet package as affected, 10.0.0 through 10.0.9 for .NET 10, fixed in 10.0.10 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2p3q-h3hg-jcqq, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/411, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/67786, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.10/10.0.10.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. No file in these packages has Negotiate in its name or path: there is no Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate.dll and no Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate nupkg. The Negotiate handler is distributed as a separate NuGet package and is not part of the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework that aspnetcore10-runtime carries, and the source-built nupkg set in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts does not include it. The same scan found the other ASP.NET Core assemblies by name, for example Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.dll at the build's own version in every build, so the search itself works. An application that needs Negotiate authentication adds the package from NuGet itself, and is then covered by Microsoft's advisory for that package, not by this owner.

CVE-2026-47303 (GHSA-2p3q-h3hg-jcqq) is an elevation of privilege issue in the ASP.NET Core Negotiate authentication handler caused by improper parsing. Microsoft lists only the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate NuGet package as affected, 9.0.0 through 9.0.17 for .NET 9, fixed in 9.0.18 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2p3q-h3hg-jcqq, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/411, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.18/9.0.18.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. None of these packages contains Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate.dll or a Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Negotiate nupkg. The Negotiate handler is distributed as a separate NuGet package and is not part of the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework that aspnetcore9-runtime and the SDK in dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap carry, and the source-build nupkg set in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts does not include it. The same scan found the other ASP.NET Core assemblies by name (for example Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.dll at the build's version in every build), so the search itself works. An application that needs Negotiate authentication must add the package from NuGet itself, and is then covered by Microsoft's advisory for that package, not by this owner.
